summary: The root خمص (khmS) primarily describes emptiness or hunger, especially of the belly. It can refer to a person who is hungry or lank, and metaphorically, one who abstains from others' possessions.
lane: خَمِيصٌ خميص Empty; applied to the belly: (TA:) hungry. (Msb.) -b2- خَمِيصُ البَطْنِ , (A,) or خَمِيصُ الحَشَا , (S, K,) and , (S, A, K,) and , (A, K,) A man empty in the belly, (A,) or lank in the belly; (S, K;) as also البَطْنِ : (K * and TA in art. رهف :) and slender in make: (TA:) fem. of the first with ة , (S, A, K,) and so of the second, (Yaakoob, S, A, K,) and so of the third; (TA;) and IAar mentions as a fem., occurring prefixed to الحَشَا in a verse of El-Asamm Ed-Dubeyree: (TA:) pl., (S, A, K,) masc., (A, K,) خِمَاصٌ ; (S, A, K;) and fem., [i. e., of خميصة ,] خَمَائِصُ : (A, K:) has no pl. formed by the addition of و and ن , though its fem. is formed by the addition of ة ; being made to accord with the measure فَعْلَانٌ , of which the fem. is فَعْلَى . (TA.) خِمَاصٌ [also] signifies Hungry, in a pl. sense, (K,) and lank in the bellies: (TA:) also signifies the same as خَمِيصٌ ; and [its pl.] مَخَامِيصُ , lank in the bellies ( خُمْصُ البُطُونِ [whence it appears that , sing. of خُمْصٌ , is also syn. with خَمِيصٌ ]). (TA.) You say also, هُوَ خَمِيصُ البَطْنِ مِنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ , meaning (tropical:) He is one who abstains from [ devouring ] the possessions of men. (A.) And خِمَاصُ البُطُونِ مِنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ خِفَافُ الظُّهُورِ مِنْ دَمَائِهِمْ , (A, TA,) meaning (tropical:) Persons who abstain from [ devouring ] the possessions of men, whose backs are light with respect to [ the ] burden [ of their blood ]. (TA, from a trad.) -b3- زَمَنٌ خَمِيصٌ (tropical:) A time of hunger. (A, TA.)

headwords.def: خَمِصَتِ القَدَمُ خمصت القدم, aor. خَمَصَ, inf. n. خَمَصٌ, The man's foot rose from the ground, [or was hollow in the middle of the sole, ] so that it did not touch it. (Msb.) خَمَصَ البَطْنُ, (A, K,) aor. خَمُصَ; (TK;) and خَمِصَ, aor. خَمَصَ; and خَمُصَ, aor. خَمُصَ; (A, K, TK;) inf. n. خمص [i. e. خَمْصٌ or خُمْصٌ or probably both] and خُمُوصٌ and مَخْمَصَةٌ; (TK;) The belly was, or became, empty; (A, K, TK;) i. e., hungry: (TK:) [and lank: see خَمِيصٌ.] And خَمُصَ الشَّىْءُ, aor.

تخامص عَنْهُ تخامص عنه تخامص عنة (tropical:) He shrank, or drew away, from it; (A, K; *) i. e., from anything of which he disliked the nearness. (A.) You say, مَسَسْتُهُ بِيَدِى وَهْىَ بَارِدَةٌ فَتَخَامَصَ مِنْ بَرْدِ يَدِى (tropical:) [ I touched him with my hand, it being cold, and he shrank from the coldness of my hand ]. (A, TA.) تَخَامَصْ لِفُلَانٍ عَنْ حَقِّهِ (tropical:) [ Relinquish thou, i. e.,] give thou, to such a one, his right, or due. (A, K.

خَمْصَةٌ خمصه خمصة A hungering. (S, K.) You say, لَيْسَ لِلْبَطْنَةِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ خَمْصَةٍ تَتْبَعُهَا [ There is not anything better for repletion of the belly than a hungering which follows it ]. (S, A.)
خُمْصَانٌ خمصان: see أَخْمَصُ: and see also خَمِيصٌ, in two places.

خَمِيصٌ خميص Empty; applied to the belly: (TA:) hungry. (Msb.) خَمِيصُ البَطْنِ, (A,) or خَمِيصُ الحَشَا, (S, K,) and, (S, A, K,) and, (A, K,) A man empty in the belly, (A,) or lank in the belly; (S, K;) as also البَطْنِ: (K * and TA in art. رهف:) and slender in make: (TA:) fem.

خَمِيصَةٌ خميص خميصه خميصة A [ garment of the kind called ] كِسَآء, black, square, and having عَلَمَانِ [i. e. two ornamental or coloured or figured borders ]: (S, A, Mgh, K:) or a black كساء, having a border such as is above described ( مُعْلَم ) at each end, and which is of خَزّ, [q. v.], or of wool: (Msb:) if not bordered, it is not so called: (S, Msb:) or, accord.
خَامِصُ البَطْنِ خامص البطن: see خَمِيصٌ.

أَخْمَصُ القَدَمِ A man whose foot rises from the ground, [or is hollow in the middle of the sole, ] so that it does not touch it: fem. خَمْصَآءُ: and pl. خُمْصٌ: (Msb:) and signifies having the middle of the sole of the foot moderately rising from the ground; which is a goodly quality; but when it is flat, or rises much, it is dispraised: so explained by IAar when he was asked by Th respecting 'Alee's saying of Mohammad, [cited, but not explained, in the K,] كَانَ خُمْصَانَ الأَخْمَصَيْنِ:…

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
